messages:
maria.g: Nightly eval tripped on 3 regression prompts — outputs became shorter and more generic. Spike shows up in last two runs. Anybody else seeing a sampling param change?

devon_w: Yup I noticed. Shorter answers, truncated completions. My quick diff of the runner config shows a templating tweak yesterday around the sampling defaults.

eval-bot: nightly-eval v2.14 finished — failures: 3, pass: 97, commit: 5f3b2c8, job_id: nightly-eval-2026-03-20-02 — artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/nightly/v2.14/results.json

maria.g: Can you paste the runner config snippet? wondering if top_p/top_k or temp were implicitly changed.

devon_w: snippet from deploy config that landed in 5f3b2c8:
```yaml
model: rwd-open-7b-quant
sampling:
  temperature: ${SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE:-0.0}  # accidentally defaulted to 0.0
  top_p: ${SAMPLING_TOP_P:-0.92}
  top_k: ${SAMPLING_TOP_K:-50}
```

kai: If temp is defaulting to 0.0 that's a smoking gun — deterministic greedy output. Why would env var be missing? CI template change?

sophia: I saw a change in the deploy template where we moved to env-less defaults to enforce reproducibility for evals. Guess that forced temperature to 0.0 for many workers.

maria.g: That aligns with outputs. The failing prompts show much shorter reply lengths and repeated stop tokens. We should repro locally with temp 0.0 vs 0.7.

devon_w: quick reproduce commands I ran:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-open-7b-quant","prompt":"Explain recursion in five sentences","temperature":0.0}'
# vs
curl -X POST ... "temperature":0.7
```
Outputs differ dramatically — 0.0 truncates earlier and prefers safer phrases.

eval-bot: uploaded failing generations -> s3://redwood-evals/nightly/v2.14/fails/ (3 files).

kai: I'll bisect the deploys to find when the template change propagated to the runner fleet. Starting with these commits: 5f3b2c8 (suspect), 5e8a7b1 (previous).

maria.g: Tagging this as a regression. Can we run a patched eval with temp=0.7 to confirm recovery? If yes, we should rollback templating change for nightly runs only.

devon_w: Running a quick patched job now with environment override SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=0.7 — queue id: patch-eval-196543. I'll post results when done.

sophia: Also double-check top_p/top_k defaults — they might interact with low temp to shorten completions.

kai: FYI the templating change was intended to remove env leakage for reproducible infra tests, but we accidentally applied it to prod nightly evals. Will scope it to ci-only.

eval-bot: patch-eval-196543 completed — pass: 99, failures: 1, job_id: patch-eval-196543, artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/patch-eval/196543/result.json

maria.g: Nice — looks like temp override largely fixes the regression. Which prompt still failing?

devon_w: One prompt is sensitive to top_p=0.92 vs 0.98. I reran with temp=0.7 top_p=0.98, that recovered the last fail.

sophia: Proposed short-term fix: set explicit nonzero sampling defaults in the nightly job manifest and revert the template change for prod-nightly. Long-term: add an eval-guard that warns if sampling config is deterministic.

kai: I'll open a roll-forward PR to change the template scoping and add a manifest override for nightly.

maria.g: I'll file an eval ticket to add an automated check (detect temp<=0.01 && top_p<0.95) and fail the pipeline with a warning.

devon_w: Assigning follow-ups: infra#4321 (template scoping), eval#212 (guard check).

sophia: Thanks everyone. Quick win validated. :tada:

maria.g: Thanks — moving to postmortem-ish note and closing the triage.
